content_of_post_to_answer: Christian Slater says that he's used to moving fast because he grew up in New York. In what ways do you think your upbringing shaped your personality and habits?
answer: Growing up in a place like New York can train more than your pace; it can shape your sense of attention, independence, and how quickly you read situations. But the interesting part is that traits we call personality are often adaptations to our environment. Speed can become efficiency, but it can also become impatience. The places that raise us give us strengths, but they also quietly teach us habits we may need to unlearn.
